title: Throughput field-runner and customer scenario certification for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Sofia Reyes
description: Build and validate a deterministic field-runner for Dedicated Capacity that can replay representative customer traffic patterns, measure throughput/latency with structured percentiles, and certify customer acceptance scenarios. Focus on hybrid workloads (sync text generation + async embeddings), KV-cache warmup behaviors, and autoscaler hysteresis under bursty arrivals.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity ask for throughput guarantees and predictable tail latency under mixed workloads. Existing synthetic prober runs steady-state token streams and separate stress tests; they miss subtle behaviors caused by KV-cache cold starts, multi-model fallbacks, autoscaler hysteresis, and realistic inter-arrival burst patterns. We need a field-proven harness that can 1) ingest captured traces, 2) deterministically replay them against a candidate fleet, and 3) generate a customer-facing certification report with pass/fail criteria and recommended autoscaler settings.
goals: Implement a replayable field-runner that accepts trace bundles and a simple mapping layer to translate real requests to our test harness
Define a benchmark matrix that covers steady-state, warmup, burst, and degradation modes across model sizes and quantization profiles
Provide a reproducible customer acceptance checklist and artifacts (dashboards, CSVs, verdict summary)
out_of_scope: Full end-to-end billing reconciliation for load tests and integration with external SIEMs. Production autoscaler code changes (this ticket focuses on harness + recommendations; autoscaler code changes will be separate tickets)
approach: Trace ingestion: translator for anonymized request traces (header normalization, prompt templates, token lengths)
Deterministic replay: deterministic RNG seeding, deterministic queue ordering, and optional inter-arrival time scaling
Hybrid workload modeling: compose mixed streams (generation, embeddings, rerank) with tunable ratios
KV-cache warmup protocol: configurable warmup phase, measured cache hit curve, and recommended warmup durations
Autoscaler sweep harness: run parameter sweeps for scale-up/scale-down thresholds and hysteresis windows, measure oscillation and SLA violations
Customer report generator: auto-generate a one-page summary plus per-run artifacts (latency percentiles, p95/p99 token throughput, error classes)
Acceptance automation: a pass/fail evaluator using the acceptance criteria below
test_matrix: Steady-state read-heavy: 100 RPS, 60% embeddings, 40% small-gen (<=128 tokens) on model-x-small
Warmup-to-steady: cold KV cache then ramp from 0 to target over 6 minutes
Bursty arrival: Poisson baseline + 30s bursts at 5x baseline every 10 minutes
Mixed-size long-tail: 10% long generation (>1024 tokens) interspersed with short requests
Autoscaler hysteresis sweep: evaluate scale-down windows of 30s/60s/120s and scale-up thresholds of 70%/85%/95% utilization
measurement_methodology: Each run is composed of phases: preflight (sanity checks), warmup (KV-cache and kernel priming), steady-state (measurement window), and cooldown. We capture per-request timestamps at client, routing, and serving layers to compute: end-to-end p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, server-side token throughput, token-level tail latency, and error spectrum. For reproducibility, each benchmark is run 3 times with identical seeds and median-run selected as canonical. All raw logs and trace bundles are stored and linked in the customer artifact bundle.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p95 latency <= customer SLA for steady-state matrix
No error-class regression compared to baseline (errors per million request threshold)
Autoscaler parameter set achieves <5% SLA violations during burst tests and recovers without oscillation in 3 minutes
KV-cache warmup curve reaches >=90% steady hit-rate within the recommended warmup window
Certification report generated with reproducible artifacts and a deterministic verdict (pass/fail)
deliverables: Field-runner binary and lightweight trace translator (Docker image + run script)
A benchmark suite repo with canonical workload bundles and runner configs
Customer acceptance report template and sample reports for three canonical customers
Dashboards: throughput/latency live-view and post-run summarized views
Runbook for solutions engineers to execute customer certification and interpret results
milestones: 2025-11-18: Prototype runner that can replay anonymized traces against local dev cluster
2025-11-22: Add autoscaler sweep harness and basic KV-cache metrics
2025-11-29: Integrate report generator and produce sample customer report
2025-12-05: Validate against 3 partner customers in private preview
risks: Trace fidelity: captured customer traces may omit internal timing information and require heuristics to map to runner events
Determinism limitations: certain runtime kernels and non-deterministic GPU scheduling could add run-to-run variance
Resource cost: exhaustive sweeps across model variants and scale configurations are expensive to run at fleet scale
False sense of safety: passing synthetic replay may not capture live multi-tenant noise
notes_and_decisions: 11/13: Decided to prioritize deterministic replay + seeded RNG over stochastic load generators to improve reproducibility
11/15: Chose CSV-based trace bundle format with a small JSON manifest to avoid protobuf dependency for now
11/17: Agreed to surface recommended autoscaler params, not to ship as default; ops will review before any cluster-wide change
run_instructions: Checkout repo, populate traces/ with anonymized bundles, edit config.yaml to point at target cluster, run ./run-field-runner --manifest traces/manifest.csv --seed 42 --mode replay. Use --autoscaler-sweep to run parameter sweeps. Reports are emitted to artifacts/<timestamp>/report.zip
